 These Appeals, Coming On For Admission, This
Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

MFA No.201957/2019 is by the claimant/appellant seeking enhancement of compensation and MFA No.201447/2019 is by the respondent/Corporation NC: 2023:KHC-K:8652 disputing the quantum awarded by the Tribunal in judgment and award dated 01.04.2019 passed in MVC No.107/2017 on the file of I Additional Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Kalaburagi, by which, the Tribunal while partly allowing the claim petition has awarded total compensation of Rs.11,37,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
2. Accident in question that occurred on 13.01.2016 at about 1.00 p.m. resulting in injuries to the claimant involving a motorcycle bearing Registration No.AP-28/PQ-9377 and a Bus bearing Registration No.KA- 32/F-1936
is not in dispute.

The Divisional Controller vs Koninti Balakrishna And Anr on 17 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75865935/
3 3.

entities.text: Divisional Controller vs Koninti Balakrishna And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is contended that claimant was working as a collie and was earning sum of Rs.15,000/- p.m.
and contributing the same to the family.
That due to the accident, the claimant suffered injuries resulted in amputation of right leg below knee at 1/3rd .
Disability of NC: 2023:KHC-K:8652 the claimant to the right lower limb has been assessed at 60%.
The tribunal taking into consideration of the material evidence placed on record has awarded compensation as noted above.
4. Sri.

Veeranagouda Malipatil, learned counsel for the appellant/claimant in MFA No.201957/2019 reiterating the grounds urged in the memorandum of appeal submits that tribunal has grossly erred in assessing the income of the claimant at Rs.7,500/- p.m., which is on the lower side.
He further submits that grant of compensation on other heads is also on a lower side.
Hence, seeks for allowing of the appeal by enhancing compensation.

5. On the other hand, Smt.Sangeeta Bhadrashetty, learned counsel appearing for the appellant/respondent/Corporation in MFA No.201447/2019 vehemently opposes that assessment of the disability of the claimant at 60% considering the nature of the injury is exorbitant.

She referring to the Schedule-I of the NC: 2023:KHC-K:8652 Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 submits that nature of injury being amputation of the leg below right knee which is just about 1/3rd of a limb, same has been statutorily assessed at 50% and same ought to have been adopted by the tribunal.
She also submits that the Tribunal failed to appreciate that the rider of the motorcycle was proceeding with two other occupants and the negligence ought to have been attributed on him as well.

Further, she submits that assessment of income in the absence of any documentary evidence is just and proper and does not warrants any interference and grant of compensation on the other heads are also just and proper warranting no interference.
Thus, she submits that assessment of disability has to be reduced while granting compensation.

Hence, seeks for allowing of the appeal filed in MFA No.201447/2019.
6.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
Since the accident in question is not in dispute, the only issue which requires to be considered is with regard to the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
The fact that the offending bus had hit the motorcycle from behind is not in dispute.

Merely because the rider of the motorcycle was proceeding with two other occupants on the motorcycle, would not itself amount to negligence,
it may at the most amount to violation of rules.
The same is not sufficient enough to attribute negligence on the part of the injured.
As per Ex.P6 - Discharge Summary the claimant has been diagnosed with traumatic hind foot amputation right and has been given treatment of electric amputation below right knee.

As per the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, Part-II, item Nos. 22 and 23, amputation of one foot resulting in hind wearing as well as amputation below knee with stump exceeding 12.70 cm is shown as 50%.
8. Tribunal relying upon the evidence and medical evidence of PW.2 has assessed disability at 60%.

4 NC: 2023:KHC-K:8652

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering the nature of the injury and amputation being below knee applying the standards set out in the schedule referred to the above, disability is assessed at 50%
instead of 60%.
The claim of the claimant to has been earning of Rs.15,000/- p.m. and no documentary evidence is produced in this regard.
In the absence of material evidence and considering the accident is of the year 2016, Rs.8,750/- has taken into consideration as per chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
9 . In the complaint as well as in the medical records, the age of the claimant is shown as 25 years.
Learned counsel for the respondent /Corporation vehemently submits that mother of the claimant in her complaint-Ex.P1 has stated that the age of the claimant is 26 years.
Thus, she submits that multiplier '17' is applicable and not '18' as taken by the tribunal.

Since the mother of the claimant herself has stated in her complaint that age of the claimant at 26 years and same has been NC:
2023:KHC-K:8652 relied upon by the tribunal, age of the claimant has to be taken as '26' years instead of 25 years.

10. In view of the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Erudaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Limited reported in AIR 2020 Supreme Court 4284, has held that even in injury cases, claimant would be entitled for addition of future prospects.

entities.text: Erudaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Limited reported in AIR 2020 Supreme Court 4284
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since disability sustained by claimant is substantial and considering age of claimant as 26 years from medical records, it would be appropriate to add 40% towards future prospects.

Since the disability is assessed at 50%
claimant is also entitled for future prospects at 40%.
11. Calculated as above the claimant would be entitled for a sum of Rs.12,49,500/-.

[Rs.8,750/- +
(40% future prospects)= Rs.12,250/-]
(a) The tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.60,000/- towards 'pain and suffering', same is - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:8652 maintained.

The tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.20,000/-
towards 'Medical expenses' same is maintained.
The tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.2,400/- towards 'food and extra nourishment and medical attendant', same is enhanced to Rs.25,000/-.The
tribunal
has awarded compensation of Rs. 10,000/- towards 'conveyance', same is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.
The tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs. 22,500/- towards 'loss of income during treatment', same is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.
Loss of income during treatment period is awarded Rs.22,250/- same is enhanced to Rs.26,250/- (Rs.8,750 X3 months).
The tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards 'Deprivation of future amenities', same is enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-.

12. Thus, in total the appellant/claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,10,750/- instead of Rs.11,37,000/- as awarded by the Tribunal, which is as under:

ORDER a) The appeals filed in MFA No.201957/2019 and in MFA No.201447/2019 are partly allowed.

e) The award of the Tribunal is modified accordingly.
